title: Hard-coded JWT signing secret
description: The application uses a source-controlled, fixed value as the HS256 signing key. Anyone who obtains the repository can mint valid authentication tokens, including tokens for staff accounts.

title: Passwordless token refresh accepts unsigned JWT claims
description: The refresh endpoint disables signature verification and trusts the supplied sub claim before issuing a newly signed token. An unauthenticated attacker can submit an unsigned JWT naming any existing user and obtain a valid token for that account, including a staff account.
evidence: claims = jwt.decode(token, options={"verify_signature": False}); user = load_user(claims.get("sub")); return jsonify(token=make_token(user))

title: Unauthenticated unsafe deserialization of basket cookie
description: The basket cookie is entirely client-controlled and is passed to pickle.loads without authentication or a restricted unpickler. A crafted cookie can execute arbitrary Python code when any visitor requests /basket.

title: Order detail endpoint exposes other customers' orders
description: The authenticated order-detail endpoint calls get_order directly and never checks that the order belongs to the requesting user. Any logged-in customer who guesses an order ID can read another customer's items, payment totals, status, and refunds.

title: Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection
description: The public search query is concatenated into a SQL statement instead of being bound as a parameter. An attacker can alter the WHERE clause and extract or manipulate data through the search endpoint.
evidence: "SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%" + q + "%' OR sku LIKE '%" + q + "%' ORDER BY name LIMIT 50"

title: Stored review content is rendered as trusted HTML
description: Review bodies are accepted from authenticated users and later rendered with the Jinja safe behavior in the product template. A reviewer can store script or event-handler markup that executes for users viewing the product page.
evidence: The review body is inserted at line 90 and rendered as {{ r.body|safe }} in shopapi/templates/product.html line 14.

title: Payment timeout is treated as successful payment
description: If the payment provider times out, the application unconditionally changes the order to processing and records the full total as paid. A provider outage or induced timeout can therefore create unpaid orders that are fulfilled.
evidence: except requests.Timeout: ... status = "paid"; the paid branch sets status = 'processing' and paid_pence = total_pence

title: Payment webhook signature does not cover payment amount or status
description: The HMAC is calculated only over order_id, while the handler trusts attacker-controlled status and amount_pence fields. Any party able to obtain or reuse a valid order signature can change the credited amount, including crediting an order as paid for zero or an arbitrary amount.
evidence: webhook_signature(order_id) signs only str(order_id), but lines 247-249 trust event status and int(event.get("amount_pence", 0))

title: Approved-host image import follows unrestricted redirects
description: The URL is checked against the approved host and public DNS result once, then requests.get follows redirects by default. An approved host can redirect the server to an internal or metadata-service address, allowing staff-triggered SSRF and retrieval of internal responses.
evidence: check_url(url) validates the initial URL, then requests.get(url, timeout=10, stream=True) follows redirects without allow_redirects=False or validating each destination

title: Customer display names enable second-order SQL injection in review reports
description: A staff report interpolates a customer's mutable display_name directly into SQL. A customer can set a display name containing SQL syntax; when staff request that customer's report, the injected expression is executed and can disclose review data beyond the selected customer.
evidence: f"WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}' ORDER BY r.id DESC"

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes
description: Password hashing uses a single unsalted SHA-256 digest with no work factor or password-hashing KDF. A database disclosure permits efficient offline cracking of users' passwords, including reused passwords.
